limitations: Small, hand-curated panel (10 targets, 30 actives, 60 decoys) — not a substitute for DUD-E or large-scale virtual screens.
Decoys are other approved drugs, so all compounds are drug-like; separation is harder than vs random SMILES.
Decoys were not property-matched to actives (MW/logP), so some baselines may look better or worse than in matched decoy sets.
On-target labels come from primary indications / pharmacology tables encoded in TargetForge rules, not from fresh IC50 measurements.
Co-crystal ligand identity bonuses can inflate scores for exact reference matches (e.g., erlotinib on 1M17).
pipeline_notes: Scored with `rankCandidatesLocal` / `scoreOne` from `src/scoreCandidates.js` (source: heuristic-v2) — identical to local Staging Bench and repurposing batch numeric ranks.
PAINS/toxicophore checks run via `checkPainsFast` on supplied SMILES (same patterns as the bench).
OpenAI `/api/rank-candidates` reasoning is excluded so results stay deterministic and reproducible.
RDKit WASM ADME (`admeCalculator.js`) and organ-toxicity flags are not combined into the 0–100 ranking score in production; they were not applied here.
Native docking baseline uses `runMolecularDocking` (via `src/benchmark/dockingBench.test.js` + RDKit WASM) with searchExhaustiveness=4 and seeded Math.random per (PDB, CID).
interpretation: On this 10-target panel, TargetForge's deterministic target-aware heuristic (30 labeled actives) achieved mean ROC-AUC 1 with top-1 hit rate 100.0% (37.1% expected by chance on these class priors). That near-perfect separation is expected: the benchmark labels are the same drug-name lists encoded in `TARGET_RULES`, so the test largely verifies lookup consistency rather than predictive binding. By contrast, the empirical docking baseline (mean ROC-AUC 0.506, top-1 28.6%) is only slightly better than chance on this small set and is **not** wired into the 0–100 Staging Bench score. RDKit ADME and organ-toxicity modules are likewise separate. For portfolio messaging, cite the heuristic panel result as "rule-table consistency on curated actives vs approved decoys," not as prospective virtual-screening accuracy.
